pr_body:
Make sure all commands check to see if there are any "extra" arguments
after the options, and print an error if so.

Made all error messages consistent (which is to say, minimal).

Fixes: #13527
pr_comments: Reviews aside, this is good work, thanks for doing it
CI failures in sanitizers seem unrelated.
This pull request is ready to merge
Merged to master. Thank you for the contribution.

issue_context.title: APPS: Check that all apps really consume all command line arguments
issue_context.body: As part of this, the apps need to check if there are any remaining command line arguments, and exit with an error in that case
comments: Almost all commands do this.  Some (cms, errstr) are special cases.  Which ones have you found?

> Which ones have you found?

We haven't.  We made this issue as a reminder to double check.  Are you willing to help us out with this?
Yes, I will do this, to help 3.0 get done.

review_comments:
````
openssl dhparam 
````
Gives an error for me locally, since it requires the generator (e.g -2) to be set in order to set a default bitsize.. That is a bit weird.
I get an error from 1.1.1 "can't load params" 3.0 plain and this branch do the same thing.  What error do you see that is unexpected?

The point is it says that the bitsize is an optional parameter. So if you dont specify it, it should just choose a default one. This is not what it does - it exits unless you also specify another optional param i.e '-2'.
So it should either
(1) choose a default generator + bitsize OR
(2) print an error specifying that one of the generator params is required..

I didn't change the behavior about this stuff. It looks to me (line 163/164) that if you're generating something it does use a default bitsize. The manpage describes behavior that is weird.  But I don't think changing the way it works is something to do in this PR.
It does look a bit curious to have `OPT_ERR` jump to `opthelp`, directly followed by an `OPT_HELP`...  that doesn't.
Yes.  It took untangling the previous goto/goto stuff to make that obvious :)  I put the opthelp body inside the switch, just like the other commands.  Curiosity solved :)
I wonder if it should be printing 'reading from stdin' for the case when -in is not specified.
I would prefer not to add verbosity like that; none of the other commands (e.g., x509 etc) do this.
I was thinking from the perspective of a user who it presented with a cursor after doing this. Probably out of scope here..
I'd recommend not adding this printing (if ever, it should be printed to stderr) as people definitely depend on using openssl as filter and not printing things that they do not expect print.
